meta.notes: Source of truth for the history layer. Frames are snapshots, not a continuous scrub: the archives support dated moments, not annual geometry. Dot anchors are [lon, lat] EPSG:4326 and the site projects them, same as trivia. verified:false frames render a draft flag on the card until the fact-check pass clears them. ship:false frames appear on the scrubber and say they are still being inked.
honesty_footnotes: Past market footprints are drawn with today's utility shapes. Distribution boundaries move far less than market membership, but this is an approximation.
Empire tints show where a holding company had subsidiaries. That is reach, not exclusive territory, and the empires overlapped.
The line between the Eastern and Western grids is drawn from today's utility boundaries. It settled roughly here by the mid-1970s.
meta.dots_note: The 50 largest urban places of the 1900 Census, every one of which had central-station service, plus four small places that were firsts. Populations are read from the Census table, not transcribed. Generated by pipeline/11-build-timeline-dots.mjs.

frames.title: Islands of light
frames.body: In 1900 there was no grid. There were thousands of small ones. A power station lit the blocks around it and stopped. If you lived past the last wire, you had no electricity at all. Every glowing dot here is a city with its own station.
frames.note: The first stations ran on direct current. It could not travel far before the copper cost more than the electricity was worth, so a station lit the blocks around it and stopped. That one limit is why the map is dots instead of country.

legend.label: A city with its own power station

frames.title: A handful of men own the lights
frames.body: Small companies got bought, then the buyers got bought. By 1930 a few holding companies controlled electricity across dozens of states. Samuel Insull's system alone reached into more than twenty. The first power pool also starts here: in 1927 three Pennsylvania and New Jersey companies agreed to share their plants, and that agreement is the ancestor of PJM.
frames.verify_notes: Needs holdings-1930.json: which states each empire reached, cited per state pair. Riskiest sourcing item in the timeline.

frames.title: Texas wires itself together and stops at the border
frames.body: The war needed aluminum, steel and ships, and all of it needed power. Utilities strung lines to each other to share load. Texas companies connected to each other and deliberately not to anyone else. Staying inside one state kept them out of reach of federal regulators, and that choice still shapes the map today.
frames.verify_notes: Needs the derived interconnection seam from ba-interconnections.json, plus verification of the Texas Interconnected System formation dates.

frames.title: The country becomes one machine
frames.body: In February 1967 federal engineers closed the last ties between East and West. For the first time the whole country ran as a single synchronized machine. It did not work. The link tripped apart as often as a dozen times a day. After about eight years the ties came out.
frames.verify_notes: Tie locations, closure date and the trip frequency all need sourcing. Frame ships without tie dots if they cannot be pinned.

frames.title: The country settles for three
frames.body: The AC ties came out and went back as direct current, which lets power cross without the two sides having to stay in step. America chose to be three machines instead of one: East, West, and Texas. Power still crosses between them, but only through a few converter stations.
frames.verify_notes: Tie removal date and Pacific Intertie in-service date need sourcing.

frames.title: The referees arrive
frames.body: A federal order in 1996 said that a company owning transmission had to let competitors use it on the same terms. Somebody neutral had to run the traffic. Within a few years California, New England, New York, Texas and the Pennsylvania pool all had one. Most of the country did not, and still does not.
frames.verify_notes: Needs membership-events.json and regions.topo.json. Founding dates for CAISO, ISO-NE, NYISO and PJM's ISO transition are all flagged in the sourcing memo.

frames.title: The markets get big
frames.body: PJM swallowed the Midwest one utility at a time. Chicago joined in 2004, then Ohio, then Virginia. MISO started its own energy market in 2005. This is when the map stops being a few coastal experiments and becomes most of the eastern half of the country.
frames.verify_notes: PJM zone integration dates come from Monitoring Analytics State of the Market Appendix A. Four flagged dates should clear in one pass.

frames.title: The largest single day on the map
frames.body: On one day in December 2013, Entergy and its neighbours moved into MISO. A market that ran from Minnesota to Indiana suddenly reached the Gulf of Mexico, in a piece that does not touch the rest of it. Nothing else in the modern era moved this much ground at once.
frames.verify_notes: Needs the MISO South roster resolved to HIFLD ids and reviewed.

frames.label: Today
frames.title: Where it landed
frames.body: Seven market operators, and about a third of the country with none at all. Texas still runs its own grid on purpose, which is the 1941 decision still holding. The newest change is on the other side: in April 2026 a group of western utilities switched on a second SPP market, so one referee now runs markets on both sides of the great seam.
frames.note: This is the same picture as the Wholesale layer. Step back through the scrubber and watch it come apart.

dots.note: The 27th largest city in the country, and today it is Pittsburgh's North Side. Pittsburgh annexed it in 1907 over the objections of its own voters.
Boston, Cambridge, Somerville and Lynn are four separate cities on this map because they were four separate cities, each buying its own light.

pearl-street-1882.title: Pearl Street switches on
pearl-street-1882.body: Edison's station in lower Manhattan started up with about 85 customers and roughly 400 lamps. It served the First District, a quarter of a square mile between Wall Street and the East River. Low-voltage direct current could not reach much past that without costing more in copper than the electricity was worth.

appleton-1882.title: A water wheel in Wisconsin
appleton-1882.body: A water-driven Edison dynamo on the Fox River at Appleton lit a paper mill and a house. Customers paid a flat monthly fee per lamp, because nobody had invented a meter for this yet.
appleton-1882.note: Often called the first hydroelectric central station. The narrower claim is the true one: the first hydroelectric station running Edison's incandescent system for paying customers. Its own station building opened that November, and Grand Rapids had been selling water-powered arc light since 1880.

great-barrington-1886.title: Alternating current works
great-barrington-1886.body: William Stanley lit about twenty shops and offices along Main Street in Great Barrington. He sent alternating current down the street at 500 volts and used transformers in the basements to bring it down to 100. That is the trick a grid runs on: push the voltage up to travel, bring it down to use.
great-barrington-1886.note: An experiment, not a utility. Stanley ran it out of an old rubber mill and shut it down by that summer. The town's electric company came two years later.

telluride-1891.title: Power sent over a mountain
telluride-1891.body: The Ames plant sent 3,000 volts of alternating current 2.6 miles through the San Juan Mountains to a 100-horsepower motor at the Gold King mine. It is the first time anyone generated, moved and then actually used AC to turn machinery.
telluride-1891.note: The day is disputed: June 19 is the date usually given, and one local account says June 21. Longer AC lines already existed, at Willamette Falls in Oregon. What was new here is the industrial motor at the far end.

niagara-buffalo-1896.title: Niagara reaches Buffalo
niagara-buffalo-1896.body: Just after midnight, 1,000 horsepower from a single generator at the falls travelled 26 miles at 11,000 volts to Buffalo, where it ran the city's street railway. After this, a power station no longer had to sit inside the city it served.
niagara-buffalo-1896.note: The first current went down the line at 8:57 that Sunday evening and reached Buffalo one minute after midnight, which met a contract deadline of on or before November 15.

pjm-pool-1927.title: The first power pool
pjm-pool-1927.body: Three companies in Pennsylvania and New Jersey agreed to run their plants as one and share the savings. PJM still carries their initials.

insull-collapse-1932.title: The biggest empire falls over
insull-collapse-1932.body: Samuel Insull's pyramid of holding companies collapsed in the Depression and wiped out small investors. Congress went looking for a fix.

puhca-1935.title: Congress breaks up the empires
puhca-1935.body: The Public Utility Holding Company Act forced the pyramids apart and mostly confined a utility to one region. It also set up the split that still runs the map: states regulate the wires to your house, Washington regulates power crossing state lines.

federal-power-act-1935.title: Federal power over interstate lines
federal-power-act-1935.body: The same 1935 law gave a federal commission authority over electricity sold across state lines. Texas took note.

tis-1941.title: Texas ties itself together
tis-1941.body: Texas utilities linked their systems to move wartime power, and kept every line inside the state. What crosses no state line is not interstate commerce.

northeast-blackout-1965.title: The lights go out in the Northeast
northeast-blackout-1965.body: One relay in Ontario tripped and 30 million people lost power. Connecting grids together had made a new kind of failure possible.

golden-spike-1967.title: East meets West
golden-spike-1967.body: Federal engineers closed the last alternating-current ties between the Eastern and Western grids. The country ran as one machine for the first time.
golden-spike-1967.verify_notes: Exact date and the number and location of ties both need sourcing.

nerc-1968.title: The utilities write themselves rules
nerc-1968.body: After the blackout the industry set up a council to write reliability rules for itself. Those rules only became legally binding decades later.

ac-ties-removed.title: The country goes back to being three
ac-ties-removed.body: The alternating-current ties came out. Direct-current converter stations replaced them, which let power cross without the two grids having to stay in step.

purpa-1978.title: Somebody else is allowed to build a power plant
purpa-1978.body: PURPA made utilities buy power from independent generators. It is the first crack in one company owning the whole chain.

epact-1992.title: Wholesale competition, on paper
epact-1992.body: The Energy Policy Act let independent generators sell wholesale and let them ask for transmission access. Asking was still not the same as getting.

order-888-1996.title: Open the wires
order-888-1996.body: FERC ordered every transmission owner to offer competitors the same access it gave itself. A neutral operator was the obvious way to prove it was doing so.

ercot-iso-1996.title: ERCOT becomes a referee
ercot-iso-1996.body: Texas turned its reliability council into an independent system operator, the first in the country.

caiso-1998.title: California opens a market
caiso-1998.body: California split its utilities apart and opened a power exchange. Two years later the market failed badly enough to end retail choice in the state.

nyiso-1999.title: New York's pool becomes an operator
nyiso-1999.body: The New York Power Pool, formed after the 1965 blackout, turned into NYISO.

order-2000-1999.title: FERC asks everyone to join one
order-2000-1999.body: Order 2000 invited every transmission owner into a regional operator. It invited rather than required, which is why a third of the map still has none.

comed-2004.title: Chicago joins PJM
comed-2004.body: Commonwealth Edison moved into PJM, which put a piece of PJM 300 miles west of the rest of it.

aep-dayton-2004.title: AEP and Dayton join PJM
aep-dayton-2004.body: The gap between Chicago and the east filled in, and PJM became the biggest market in the country.

dominion-2005.title: Virginia joins PJM
dominion-2005.body: Dominion brought PJM to the Atlantic south of Washington.

miso-market-2005.title: MISO starts trading
miso-market-2005.body: MISO had been keeping the grid balanced since 2002. In 2005 it opened a market where power is bought and sold every five minutes.

spp-nebraska-2009.title: Nebraska joins SPP
spp-nebraska-2009.body: The only state where every utility is publicly owned put its power into a market run from Arkansas.

miso-south-2013.title: MISO reaches the Gulf
miso-south-2013.body: Entergy, Cleco, Cooperative Energy and the East Texas co-ops joined MISO on one day. The market gained a southern half that does not touch its northern one.

integrated-system-2015.title: The federal dams join a market
integrated-system-2015.body: Western Area Power Administration's upper plains system, Basin Electric and Heartland joined SPP. It was the first time a federal power agency traded inside a market.

spp-west-2026.title: One referee, both grids
spp-west-2026.body: A group of western utilities switched on a second SPP market on the Western grid. The same operator now runs markets on both sides of the seam, though power still cannot flow freely across it.

caldwell-2026.title: A town changes grids
caldwell-2026.body: Caldwell, Texas had been an Eastern-grid island inside Texas. New lines were built and it joined ERCOT.

puhca-1935.label: PUHCA, 1935
puhca-1935.citation: Public Utility Holding Company Act of 1935, Pub. L. 74-333, 49 Stat. 803.
puhca-1935.quote: Upon the expiration of one year after the beginning of the first registration period... it shall be unlawful for any registered holding company... to acquire, directly or indirectly, any security or utility asset...
puhca-1935.gloss: In plain words: stop building pyramids of companies on top of each other. Congress had just watched one collapse.

purpa-1978.label: PURPA, 1978
purpa-1978.citation: Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978, Pub. L. 95-617, section 210.
purpa-1978.quote: The Commission shall prescribe... such rules as it determines necessary to encourage cogeneration and small power production... requiring electric utilities to offer to purchase electric energy from such facilities.
purpa-1978.gloss: In plain words: if somebody else makes power, the utility has to buy it. Before this, a utility could simply refuse.

order-888-1996.label: FERC Order 888, 1996
order-888-1996.citation: FERC Order No. 888, Promoting Wholesale Competition Through Open Access, Docket Nos. RM95-8-000 and RM94-7-001.
order-888-1996.quote: All public utilities that own, control or operate facilities used for transmitting electric energy in interstate commerce [must] file open access non-discriminatory transmission tariffs... offering others the same transmission service they provide themselves.
order-888-1996.gloss: In plain words: you cannot own the only road and refuse to let competitors drive on it.

order-2000-1999.label: FERC Order 2000, 1999
order-2000-1999.citation: FERC Order No. 2000, Regional Transmission Organizations, Docket No. RM99-2-000.
order-2000-1999.quote: The Commission is... requiring that all public utilities that own, operate or control interstate transmission file a proposal to participate in a Regional Transmission Organization... or, alternatively, a description of efforts and plans to participate.
order-2000-1999.gloss: In plain words: join a regional operator, or write us a letter about why you have not. A third of the country wrote the letter.

census-1902-stations.title: Central Electric Light and Power Stations, 1902
census-1902-stations.citation: U.S. Bureau of the Census, Special Reports: Central Electric Light and Power Stations, 1902. Government Printing Office, 1905. Public domain.
census-1902-stations.note: The first national count found 3,620 stations: 2,805 owned by companies and 815 owned by towns. Three quarters of them were in places with fewer than 5,000 people. That is why this plate is drawn as dots. There was no network to draw, only stations and the blocks around them. The count leaves out plants a factory or hotel built for its own use, so the number of generators in the country was higher still.

ftc-utility-corporations.title: FTC investigation of utility corporations, 1928 to 1935
ftc-utility-corporations.citation: Federal Trade Commission, Utility Corporations, Sen. Doc. No. 92, 70th Cong., 1st Sess. (roughly 100 volumes).
ftc-utility-corporations.note: Congress ordered the FTC to take the holding companies apart on paper. The result runs to about a hundred printed volumes and is where the empire maps in this frame come from.

fpc-1964-survey.title: National Power Survey, 1964
fpc-1964-survey.citation: Federal Power Commission, National Power Survey (1964).

fpc-1970-facilities.title: Principal Electric Facilities, 1970
fpc-1970-facilities.citation: Federal Power Commission, The 1970 National Power Survey. Information to June 30, 1970.
